title: Merchant Shipping Act, 2007
gazette_number: Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette / Act No. 27 of 2007
description: An Act to repeal the Merchant Shipping Act 1962 and provide for merchant shipping and maritime matters in Nigeria.

sections.section_title: Rules as to name of ship
sections.full_text:
(1) The Minister may make rules prescribing the circumstances in which, and the conditions subject to which the Agency's approval may be given to the registration of a ship in Nigeria by a proposed name and the rules may prescribe the form of notice to be given before the name of the ship is marked on the ship, or before the name of the ship is entered on the register, or, in the case of a change of name of a ship registered in Nigeria, before the name of the ship is altered in the register.
(2) If the Agency refuses to approve the name of a ship, the Minister may direct that the name be altered to a name approved by the Agency.

sections.section_title: Certificate to be posted on board
sections.full_text:
(1) All safety convention certificates or certified copies thereof issued in respect of a ship by or under the authority of the Minister or Agency shall be posted up in a prominent and accessible place in the ship and kept so posted up as long as the certificate remains in force and the ship is in use.
(2) The master or owner of a ship who fails to comply with subsection (1) of this section commits an offence and on conviction is liable to a fine not less than fifty thousand naira.

sections.full_text:
(1) The Minister may make regulations respecting the design, construction, testing, inspection, maintenance and use of safe containers in Nigeria, and for the implementation of the International Convention for Safe Containers, 1972, as amended from time to time.
(2) Any person who contravenes the regulations made under this section commits an offence and on conviction is liable to a fine not less than one hundred thousand naira.

In this Part of this Act -
"total loss" means an actual total loss of the vessel or such damage to the vessel that the cost of saving and repairing her would be unreasonable;
"vessel" means any ship, craft, machine, rig or platform whether of navigation or not which is involved in a collision.
(1) This Part of this Act shall apply to any person as if the expression "owner" included the person responsible for the fault of any ship.

(1) Except where otherwise provided in this Act, a prosecution for an offence under this Act shall not be instituted without the consent of the Attorney-General of the Federation.
(2) Subsection (1) of this section does not apply to offences relating to the discipline of seamen, or to offences committed by persons subject to naval or military law.

sections.full_text:
(1) Subject to the provisions of this Act, the Minister shall have the general superintendence of the matters to which this Act relates, and may designate any officer or authority for the purpose of carrying out any powers conferred upon him under this Act.
(2) The Marine Board may exercise such powers as are conferred upon it by this Act or regulations made thereunder in relation to the investigation of marine casualties and competency of certificated officers.
